title: Codex CLI da OpenAI como backend alternativo completo ao Claude (selecionavel no cam config)
description: OBJETIVO: o Codex CLI da OpenAI (comando `codex`) como alternativa COMPLETA ao `claude`: o harness inteiro roda em OU claude (+ seus modelos) OU codex (+ seus modelos), escolhido no menu de config. DEPENDE de CAM-53 (o seletor de backend + os modelos vivem la); planejar/implementar CAM-53 antes. Exige abstrair o backend atras de uma interface cobrindo: (a) invocacao do worker (claude --agent X --session-id <uuid> '<prompt>' vs a invocacao do codex); (b) deteccao de conclusao (o polling do sentinel CAM_*_STATUS / <review> no capture-pane vs o equivalente no codex); (c) modelo de sessao/agente (o codex tem seu proprio modelo de agent-definition e de resume de sessao, diferente do --agent + --session-id do claude); (d) launch da persona do orquestrador (wrapper bash do bounded-respawn). SPIKE DE DESIGN PRIMEIRO (antes de codar): mapear a CLI do codex (invocacao, sessao, output/sentinel, config de modelo/agent), identificar o que NAO mapeia pro modelo do cam, e decidir a fronteira da abstracao (uma interface BackendAdapter com claude e codex como implementacoes). ESCOPO: abstracao BackendAdapter no worker-spawn + supervisor + run.ts; adapter do codex; wiring de config (de CAM-53); os prompts dos agentes (subagent-*.md) podem precisar de forma codex-compativel; os modelos do codex sao configuraveis no menu. RELACIONA: CAM-53 (pre-req), CAM-42 (modelo de worker TUI + sentinel que precisa ser re-implementado pro codex), regra no-claude-p (revisitar o equivalente no codex). ACEITE: com backend=codex no config, `cam run`/plan/next/review/ship funcionam ponta-a-ponta no codex; backend=claude inalterado; spike de design documentado antes da implementacao; typecheck; tests.

spec.scope: Wire the OpenAI Codex CLI (the codex command) as a selectable LLM backend, a complete alternative to claude for the WORKER actors. DESIGN SPIKE FIRST (the issue demands it): the first deliverable is a design spike producing an ADR that (i) defines a BackendAdapter abstraction seam fronting the currently-claude-hardcoded spawn paths and (ii) resolves the six claude/codex mismatches; codex dispatch code lands only after the spike ADR. CAM-53 already shipped the config plumbing (backend string, default claude, ConfigScreen option labeled 'wired in CAM-54') and the runtime guard (spawn-resolution.ts:60 CODEX_GUARD_NOTICE); this issue replaces the guard's not-yet-wired behavior with real dispatch. Abstraction boundary = the report/sentinel/JSON contract (CAM_*_STATUS lines, <review> tags, worker-report.json/review-report.json), whose parsing is already backend-agnostic (report-parse.ts, ADR-0038); the BackendAdapter encapsulates spawn argv, completion detection, session/transcript model, agent-prompt injection, permission/sandbox+env, and model-id namespace. Codex runs as a TUI pane (operator steer) mirroring the claude worker model, reusing the sentinel/report contract as the completion boundary. IN SCOPE: spike ADR + BackendAdapter seam + codex wired end-to-end for the worker actors (implementer, planner, auditor, reviewer). FOLLOW-UPS (out, separate issues): orchestrator-persona (run.ts bounded-respawn wrapper), retry launcher, auth-preflight codex parity. OUT OF SCOPE entirely: ship (deterministic zero-LLM, ship-runner.ts:36). Epic-scale: expect the planner to slice heavily.
acceptanceCriteria: A design-spike ADR is written FIRST, defining the BackendAdapter abstraction seam and resolving the six claude/codex mismatches (seam; session/transcript + budget-recycle; completion-detection; agent-prompt injection; permission/sandbox+env; model-id namespace); it lands before any codex dispatch code.

A BackendAdapter abstraction fronts the worker spawn-argv builders (worker-argv.ts, plan-argv.ts, review.ts) and their loop.ts/review.ts call sites; claude is refactored into an adapter with NO behavior change (existing claude path + tests stay green).

codex is wired as a real backend for the worker actors (implementer, planner, auditor, reviewer) running as TUI panes and emitting the same CAM_*_STATUS / <review> / worker-report.json / review-report.json contract the supervisor parses; selecting backend=codex dispatches codex and the spawn-resolution guard's not-yet-wired notice is replaced by real dispatch.
The context-budget/recycle backstop behaves correctly under backend=codex per the spike's decision (a codex transcript equivalent OR a documented graceful degradation), never silently broken.
codex model ids populate the per-phase model config when backend=codex (backend-conditional ConfigScreen + models.ts) without breaking the claude tier-alias path.
Orchestrator-persona, retry launcher, and auth-preflight codex parity are OUT of scope (tracked as follow-ups); ship stays zero-LLM and unaffected.
typecheck passes, check:all is green, the claude backend path is unchanged (all existing tests pass), and new tests cover the BackendAdapter seam plus the codex argv/adapter.
gotchas: 'backend' is overloaded: the issue_system backend (local/github/linear, src/config/issue-system.ts) is a DIFFERENT concept; CAM-53/54 mean the LLM backend (claude/codex) in src/config/models.ts + src/ui/ConfigScreen.tsx.

CAM-53 shipped only config plumbing + a guard, NO abstraction: readBackend (models.ts:171-191), DEFAULTS backend:'claude' (:62-70), ConfigScreen BACKEND_OPTIONS codex labeled 'wired in CAM-54' (:131-135), CODEX_GUARD_NOTICE (spawn-resolution.ts:60, informational, still spawns claude).

Every spawn path hardcodes claude: worker-argv.ts:177-192 (implementer), plan-argv.ts:85-99 (planner) + :146-160 (auditor), review.ts:119-133 (reviewer), run.ts:252-308/:267 (orchestrator persona), claude.ts (cam claude wrapper), run-auth-preflight.ts:81, retry/launcher.ts:81-86.
ship is deterministic zero-LLM (ship-runner.ts:36, ADR-0009) -- no codex adapter needed there.

The report/sentinel/JSON contract is the portable boundary: parsing is backend-agnostic (report-parse.ts, ADR-0038); codex agents must be prompted to emit the same CAM_*_STATUS lines / <review> tags / JSON reports.

RISKIEST sub-area: the context-budget/recycle backstop hard-couples to claude's transcript (transcript/usage.ts:232-234, orch-budget.ts, orch-recycle-watch.ts) and the --session-id lowercase-uuid uuidgen respawn dance (run.ts:281-285); codex's session/transcript model differs -- the spike must decide a codex equivalent or graceful degradation.

--agent <name> -> .claude/agents/*.md (ADR-0020; the agent body IS the system prompt) has no codex analog; the spike defines codex's prompt-injection path and whether codex-shaped agent files are needed.

--permission-mode bypassPermissions must NEVER be a cam CLI flag (test/no-permission-mode-flag.test.ts); codex has its own sandbox/approval model + different nesting/auth env vars vs the CLAUDE* env-strip (worker-argv.ts:82-102).
No MCP surface exists (grep clean) and no trust-prompt handling exists (sidestepped by bypassPermissions) -- nothing to port there.
CAM-42's no-claude-p rule (subscription; TUI panes + sentinel polling, not headless -p) needs a codex equivalent decision in the spike.
Model tier aliases are claude-only (ADR-0034, models.ts DEFAULTS); codex ids are a different namespace populating the same per-phase slots when backend=codex.
No ADR/CONTEXT entry for codex or the backend-split exists yet; the spike creates the first.
domainTerms: LLM backend: the claude-vs-codex choice (src/config/models.ts backend key), distinct from the issue_system backend (local/github/linear).

BackendAdapter: the abstraction seam this issue introduces fronting spawn argv, completion detection, session/transcript model, agent-prompt injection, permission/sandbox+env, and model-id namespace for a given LLM backend.
design spike: the issue's mandated first deliverable -- a design ADR resolving the claude/codex mismatches before any codex dispatch code.
report/sentinel contract: the backend-agnostic completion+result boundary (CAM_*_STATUS lines, <review> tags, worker-report.json/review-report.json) parsed by report-parse.ts (ADR-0038).
context-budget/recycle backstop: the claude-transcript-driven subsystem (orch-budget.ts, orch-recycle-watch.ts) that recycles the orchestrator near context exhaustion; claude-shaped today.
